response.query: How to structure and pre-register radiologist reader studies (number of readers, case mix, cross-over vs parallel design, primary endpoints, and correction for multiple comparisons) for robust effect estimates?
response.answer: To structure and pre-register radiologist reader studies, use a parallel design with multiple readers and diverse case mix; define primary endpoints clearly; correct for multiple comparisons using methods like Bonferroni or false discovery rate.

Thesis at a Glance Publication Aim Method Results/Conclusion Paper I Register based study: chronic postoperative pain after TEP repair Compare the impact of fixation with non-fixation on chronic postoperative pain in men undergoing TEP repair for primary inguinal hernia Men 30–75 years with primary inguinal hernia repaired by TEP and registered in SHR analysed regarding risk for chronic pain TEP has relatively low (7.7%) occurrence of chronic pain without difference regarding chronic pain between fixed and unfixed mesh Paper II RCT: pain and quality of life at one year after surgery comparing TEP to Lichtenstein Analyse pain and quality of life at one year after surgery comparing TEP to Lichtenstein in a highly standardised setting for techniques and for surgical skills 482 men 30–75 years with primary unilateral inguinal hernia were randomised to TEP or Lichtenstein and analysed regarding risk for chronic pain Both TEP and Lichtenstein provide good results with few recurrences and normalised QoL performed using standardized methods performed by hernia specialists Paper III Register based study: sexual dysfunction after TEP repair Introducing a new questionnaire SexIHQ, easy to use for large cohorts

results.title: 21st Century Cures Act: Interoperability, Information Blocking, and ...
results.content: This final rule implements certain provisions of the 21st Century Cures Act, including Conditions and Maintenance of Certification requirements for health information technology (health IT) developers under the ONC Health IT Certification Program (Program), the voluntary certification of health IT for use by pediatric health care providers, and reasonable and necessary activities that do not constitute information blocking. An actor's practice that is implemented to maintain or improve health IT performance and that is likely to interfere with the access, exchange, or use of electronic health information will not be considered information blocking when the practice meets a condition in paragraph (a), (b), (c), or (d) of this section, as applicable to the particular practice and the reason for its implementation. As, and for the reasons, discussed earlier in this section of this preamble, the belief standard finalized in § 171.201(a) requires the actor believe the practice will “substantially reduce” a risk of harm to a patient or another natural person that would otherwise arise from the access, exchange, or use of electronic health information affected by the practice.
